_note: Chapter 2 in-game unit text, English. Translated from design/weapons.json and design/enemies.json. Proper nouns follow data/ch2/text/glossary.json. The zh fields are kept for traceability; the runtime reads only the English fields.

professions.name: Warden
professions.hint: Front-line melee. Holds ground against heavy troops, and the only unit that can stop a cavalry charge.

professions.name: Musketeer
professions.hint: Ranged unit with heavy armor-breaking shots. Slow to reload and weak in a melee.

professions.name: Outrider
professions.hint: Mounted scout. Fast, spots traps and ambushes, and gets in behind enemy archers and casters.

professions.name: Elementalist
professions.hint: Staff caster with one control spell and one damage spell. The only unit that can break an arrow volley in flight.

professions.name: Exorcist
professions.hint: Heals wounded units, and can lay dead enemies to rest so nothing raises them again.

weapons.name: Sword and Shield
weapons.attack: Quick single-target melee, faster than the Great Glaive and lighter than a knight's blade.
weapons.tradeoff: Good on the line and on the flanks, but it cannot stop a heavy charge head-on the way the Great Glaive can.

weapons.name: Great Glaive
weapons.attack: Slow overhead cut that reaches the main target and one enemy pressed against it.
weapons.tradeoff: The best weapon for stopping heavy cavalry and holding ground, but it suffers badly from arrows and from anything that gets behind it.

weapons.name: Horsecleaver
weapons.attack: A faster, more focused heavy cut than the Great Glaive, and it works well on armored targets from the side.
weapons.tradeoff: Better for killing captains and heavy infantry, and clearly worse than the Great Glaive at stopping a charge.

weapons.name: Matchlock
weapons.attack: Steady single shots with a short reload between each, with enough damage and armor-breaking for most targets.
weapons.tradeoff: A musketeer can fight with it from the day he is hired, but his armor is far lighter than a crossbowman's.

weapons.name: Five Thunders
weapons.attack: Fires five rounds in quick succession and then takes a long reload. Rounds left over can be turned on another target.
weapons.tradeoff: Heavy damage while it has rounds, then a long gap when it can do nothing at all, on a body that is easier to kill than a crossbowman's.

weapons.name: Heavy Musket
weapons.attack: Heavy single shots at a steady rhythm, harder-hitting than the Five Thunders and reloaded one round at a time.
weapons.tradeoff: Even fire with no long pause, but much weaker than the Five Thunders at pushing back a crowd.

weapons.name: Cavalry Saber
weapons.attack: Light mounted sword work, good for reaching an exposed back rank.
weapons.tradeoff: A scout from the moment he is hired, but he has no charge and cannot hold a line.

weapons.name: Lance
weapons.attack: Mounted thrust with longer reach than the saber, slow to turn and poor in a close scrap.
weapons.tradeoff: Made for hitting archers and weak flanks. It is still light horse and cannot trade head-on with Darth Lancers.

weapons.name: Three-Eyed Gun
weapons.attack: Three shots in sequence at short to medium range, then a reload.
weapons.tradeoff: Mobile enough to cut off fast enemies, but less accurate and shorter-ranged than a musketeer on foot, and riding will not refill the barrels.

weapons.name: Wind Staff
weapons.attack: Single-target wind blade at medium range, weaker over time than the old mages' spells.
weapons.tradeoff: The only weapon that can break arrows in flight. Changing staves gives that up.

weapons.name: Stone Staff
weapons.attack: Slow single-target stone blow that works more like a heavy weapon than a spell.
weapons.tradeoff: Good at slowing ground troops and punishing a known approach, but it carries no shield and does nothing about arrows.

weapons.name: River Staff
weapons.attack: A small burst of water, weak on a single target but useful against clustered light troops.
weapons.tradeoff: Covers a retreat and clears leftover ground hazards, but it gives up the wind wall and cancels no warning.

weapons.name: Wooden Bell
weapons.attack: Heals wounded allies first, and rings a weak attack when there is nobody to heal.
weapons.tradeoff: Healing and basic laying to rest from the first day, so the profession works with nothing unlocked.

weapons.name: Bronze Spirit Bell
weapons.attack: Keeps the small heal, and its bell strikes hurt soul-calling and corpse-hauling enemies more than most weapons do.
weapons.tradeoff: The expert at laying the dead to rest and cutting soul links, but poor at saving an ally who is about to fall.

weapons.name: Lotus Lantern
weapons.attack: Steady single-target healing, better than either bell, with a weak lantern attack when idle.
weapons.tradeoff: The best choice for keeping people alive, and it cannot lay the dead to rest at all.

skills.name: Hold Fast
skills.description: Cuts damage from ordinary melee attacks for a short time, but does nothing against a charge.

skills.name: Intercept
skills.description: Stuns and shoves back a light enemy that is attacking this unit.

skills.name: Horsebreaker
skills.description: Works like Hold Fast, and while braced and facing a charge, stops it dead and destroys horse and rider.

skills.name: Follow-Through
skills.description: Works like Intercept, then lands a second blow for double damage, even on heavily armored targets.

skills.name: Steady Aim
skills.description: Improves the next shot while standing still, and moving or turning starts the aim over.

skills.name: Rending Shot
skills.description: Replaces the next shot with a round that weakens an armored target for a short time.

skills.name: Scattershot
skills.description: Replaces the next shot with a spread that hits up to six enemies, and every pellet rends armor like Rending Shot.

skills.name: Heartpiercer
skills.description: Works like Steady Aim, and the shot also punches through its target into the enemy behind it, ignoring more armor.

skills.name: Scout Ahead
skills.description: Reveals nearby ambush entrances, tripwires and the direction enemies are forming up.

skills.name: Hit and Run
skills.description: Strikes a caster, thrower or officer from behind to interrupt it, then breaks away faster for a short time.

skills.name: Ride Down
skills.description: A short charge along a clear line that knocks back light infantry, but it cannot ride through a formation.

skills.name: Turnabout
skills.description: Turns in the saddle to spear a light pursuer, then needs a moment to recover.

skills.name: Thunderclap
skills.description: A loud volley that suppresses and interrupts a small group of light enemies, though it will not stop a charge.

skills.name: Barrel Bash
skills.description: Clubs a nearby enemy with the barrels and backs the rider out of contact.

skills.name: Wind Wall
skills.description: Pushes light enemies back and leaves a wall of wind that breaks up arrows in flight, but only arrows coming from the side it covers.

skills.name: Gale Blade
skills.description: Sends several blades of wind through a narrow arc, hitting a few enemies at once.

skills.name: Quicksand
skills.description: Slows everything on a small patch of ground for a short time, though a formed charge goes through it anyway.

skills.name: Stone Spikes
skills.description: Raises spikes in sequence along a fixed strip of ground after a short delay.

skills.name: Undertow
skills.description: Drags at nearby light enemies and slows them so a line can pull back, while heavy enemies are only slowed.

skills.name: Washout
skills.description: A wave of water that damages what it passes and washes out small patches of fire and blight.

skills.name: Lay to Rest
skills.description: Seals one marked enemy body nearby so nothing can raise it again.

skills.name: Ward
skills.description: Protects a front-line ally and shortens ordinary lasting effects on him.

skills.name: Requiem
skills.description: Seals several marked enemy bodies in an area at once, so none of them can be raised or hauled away.

skills.name: Sever
skills.description: Breaks an enemy's soul-calling, corpse-hauling or anchor link and keeps it from reconnecting for a short time.

skills.name: Purify
skills.description: Removes ordinary lasting effects such as plague or sundered armor from one ally.

skills.name: Shelter
skills.description: Gives one ally a small shield for a short time, usually whoever is being focused.

enemies.name: Snare Guard
enemies.description: Plants its feet and throws a weighted rope at a unit on the edge of your line, then winches the two of them together. It cannot attack while the rope holds, and the tie can be cut.

enemies.name: Corpse Dragger
enemies.description: Hooks a fallen enemy onto its back frame and hauls it away to a shaman to be raised. Seal the body first, cut the link, or kill the dragger while it walks, since it cannot carry and fight at the same time.

enemies.name: Firepot Cart
enemies.description: Stops, plants its legs and throws clay pots that leave burning ground in a fixed arc in front of it. It cannot move and throw at once, so push in from a side it is not facing.

enemies.name: Bone Moths
enemies.description: A low swarm that loses only part of itself to a single aimed shot. Scattershot, wind blades and any area spell clear it far faster than careful shooting.

enemies.name: Bone Ballista
enemies.description: Sets up facing one direction, then looses a heavy bolt down a long line that can hit two units standing in it. Spread out, push it from the side, or take the frame apart with armor-piercing rounds; a wind wall will not turn a bolt this heavy.

enemies.name: Corpse Bearer
enemies.description: A huge slow beast that carries a cage of zombies to the front, then stops and opens it. Break the cage before it unloads and the zombies inside die with it.

enemies.name: Burrower
enemies.description: Travels underground between two visible holes to cut off units that are pulling back. It has to stay above ground for a while before it can dig again, which is when to surround it.

enemies.name: Battering Ram
enemies.description: A slow engine built to break buildings, not to fight troops, and it marks the ground before it drives forward. The front is plated, so hit the side frames; it is not cavalry, and Horsebreaker does nothing to it.

enemies.name: Ironbone
enemies.description: Very tough and heavily armored, switching between throwing rock at range and smashing anything that closes. Its plates open at the seams for a moment after a throw, which is when heavy shot hurts it most.

enemies.name: Fog Lantern
enemies.description: Stops and lights its lamp, which covers that stretch of road in fog, and it can shift to another lamp post once the lamp is out. The fog clears while it moves, and it never hides a charge lane or an arrow marker.

enemies.name: Tripwire Spider
enemies.description: Sets two stakes and strings a wire between them, which slows whatever trips it and slows riders worst of all. A scout marks the stakes beforehand, and anyone can cut them down.

enemies.name: Darth Raider
enemies.description: Light horse that probes a flank, falls back to its gathering point when it meets resistance, then tries another road. It has no armor and no charge, so a shield on each flank is usually enough.

enemies.name: Darth Lancer
enemies.description: Heavy horse that forms up, commits to a straight line and runs everything down along it. Slowing or staggering will not break a charge once it is formed, so brace a Great Glaive facing the right way or step out of the lane in time.

enemies.name: Leaping Jiangshi
enemies.description: Gathers on a visible mark, jumps over the front line in one arc and lands on the open ground behind it. It can be shot out of the air, and after landing it cannot jump again for a while.

enemies.name: Blight Mother
enemies.description: Stands still and lays sacs on the ground that only give off poison gas once they ripen. Shoot a sac early and it dies harmlessly; kill the mother and the rest never ripen.

enemies.name: Anchor Bearer
enemies.description: Drops an anchor and runs a line to an altar or an elite, taking some of the damage off it. While the line is up the bearer cannot move or attack, and the link can be cut or the frame shot apart.

bosses.name: The Shore Overseer
bosses.description: Commands a formation of skeleton archers and calls their volleys. Clear his guards and focus him down; killing him cancels the volley he has not called yet, though arrows already in the air still have to be dodged.

bosses.name: Yinggou the Drowned
bosses.description: A huge waterlogged corpse that works the shallows and drags in tides that make the low ground unsafe to stand on. The water is marked before it rises and two dry roads always lead to him, and he can be hurt at any point in the fight.

bosses.name: General Jiangchen
bosses.description: A heavy commander in old armor whose great blade commits to a direction before it falls. He can order a squad of guards forward, so step out of the blade's line and hit him while they are changing position.

bosses.name: Houqing the Hexer
bosses.description: Plants cursed standards that slow how fast your units recover, sends Darth horse around the flanks and tries to raise marked bodies again. Cut the standards down, lay the bodies to rest, or go straight for him.

bosses.name: Hanba, the Drought Fiend
bosses.description: Burns lines of ground across the dry riverbed, marked before they light, and splits your position in two. Anchor bearers keep it protected, so cut their links, then follow it between the dry patches.

bosses.name: Gu Tingzhou, the Soul Ferryman
bosses.description: The shipping master behind the whole business, protected by three soul anchors in the outer harbor. Break the anchors to strip that protection and keep out of the line of his soul waves. He can be hurt throughout the fight.

_skills_note: 2026-11-06: each profession has two base skills; each advanced weapon has one upgrade skill that is a superset of one base skill ('inherits'). Wide Sweep, Sunder, Concussion Round and Burst Shell were removed for now.
